scope: Independent ETC1 RGB differential comparison and PICA ETC1A4/BCLIM integration checks; no running-game reference comparison.
algorithm: Python random.Random(0x45544331), 10000 individual cases followed by 10000 differential cases. For each case draw getrandbits(32) selectors then getrandbits(8)&~2 control byte. Individual channels each use getrandbits(8). Differential channels draw base=randrange(32), delta=randrange(max(-4,-base),min(3,31-base)+1), then encode (base<<3)|(delta&7) and set differential bit. Channels occupy high-word bits 24,16,8; the control byte occupies bits 0..7.

Serialize selector and high words with struct.pack(<II). Reverse all eight color bytes for the standard MSB-first AOSP decoder; pass original bytes to the PICA decoder. Compare every RGB byte. Then draw getrandbits(64), serialize little-endian as the eight-byte alpha prefix, and repeat. Expected alpha is ((prefix[(4*x+y)//2]>>(4*((4*x+y)%2)))&15)*17 for row-major output pixel (x,y).

Independently enumerate every base 0..31 and delta -4..3 that produces an endpoint outside 0..31, in each RGB channel, both flips and both alpha modes: 192 cases. Require unsupported-block status and all 64 sentinel output bytes unchanged. Do not compare these undefined ETC1 inputs to the wrapping AOSP decoder.

For each local sample, parse the final 40-byte CLIM/imag footer. Compare every stored color block, including padded blocks, to AOSP. Use the separate alpha oracle for format 11. Reassemble visible pixels independently: stored_width=max(8,next_power_of_two(width)); tile=(y//8)*(stored_width//8)+x//8; subblock=[[0,1],[2,3]][(y%8)//4][(x%8)//4]; read block[tile*4+subblock] pixel (x%4,y%4). Compare the entire assembled RGBA image with px_bclim_decode, then hash it.
reference_setup: Download the pinned AOSP source URL with ?format=TEXT and base64-decode to outputs/native-textures/reference/etc1.cpp. Download opengl/include/ETC1/etc1.h at the same commit with ?format=TEXT and base64-decode to outputs/native-textures/reference/ETC1/etc1.h. Verify the recorded source and header SHA-256 before compiling.
The original AOSP source is unmodified. It is C-compatible with stdbool.h injected at compilation; no reference code is vendored.
limitations: AOSP is an independent RGB block oracle. PICA alpha and tile placement use separately written oracles grounded in the pinned emulator source and fixed asymmetric tests.
No original texture bytes, downloaded reference code, or shared libraries are tracked. Sample hashes identify locally held data.
This validates decoding and documented output orientation; it does not establish an asset game role or match rendering against a running game.
